What it says is that the revised statute now prohibits the Board of Supervisors from taking final action on any item added to the agenda after a meeting has begun, unless the item is time sensitive. To ensure the rules of order comply with the statutory change, this section must be amended accordingly. So it's in the AIR report, so if we vote on it, it will be amended. Mr. Crony, do you have any comments? Yes. Thank you, Chair Randall. So I'm commenting on number 1-0, the Smart Scale Round 7 applications. I'm happy to support this item and the application process. You know, this is applying for state funding for road projects.

But I don't support the larger four-lane bypass that is being submitted. I support the mini-bypass. The four-lane larger bypass on Route 15, and it is called the Luckett's Bypass, will take 10 years to complete, cost $390 million, and take potentially 85 properties to build.

The mini-bypass will cost a fraction of the cost at around $50 million and can be completed in two to three years, providing the community and their surrounding area near-term relief from safety concerns. So I hope that the mini-bypass will be the one supported by SmartScale.

I also would like the James Monroe Highway and Lime Kilm Road intersection. I'd like both options to be looked at. There is currently a turn lane, so a missing turn lane is what is needed, I believe, at this intersection to improve safety, not a roundabout.

So I hope that SmartScale will look at both options as both options were explored in the Route 15 South safety and operations study. Regarding 1P, the design and endorsement of Evergreen Mills Road, Hoagland Mill Road, This is a safety improvement. I'm really happy to see this moving forward. There was a terrible accident at this location, and the proposed improvement, including wider shoulders, upgraded guardrails, and improved site distance will make this section of roadway safer for residents and motorists.

And lastly, item four, the memorandum of agreement for the old Arcola School apartment. I'm happy to say that the Heritage Commission participated in Section 106 about the project, and they support the project and look forward to being involved.

The gymnasium will be available as a community space, so it'll be open to the public. I think this is a win for the community because it saves a historic New Deal school that is in disrepair for needed affordable housing.

I do want to just put out that, you know, this Arcola school is on the national register and it was county owned and it is too bad that it was allowed to fall into disrepair. I think the county has a responsibility to maintain all of its historic properties.

The capital intensity factors, it's a little bit in the weeds, but the Fiscal Impact Committee on the advice of the schools have taken the schools' fees out of the capital intensity factors, meaning that developers, when they build new homes, will not be required to pay into the fund or pay any fees into the fund to build new schools.

LCPS staff advised the school board that they believe there is enough capacity within existing and under construction facilities to serve future students, and they do not anticipate needing to open any more schools to accommodate growth within the next six years. and the six years is our capital improvement program, and that likely no new schools will be needed for up to 10 years.

And so that should hopefully lower the cost of building housing in the county at least a little bit. So I was excited that we were able to do that on the FIC committee. Item 1G, Broad Run Farms Community Water Line Extension, we're putting a little bit more money in there.

Ninety-six parcels in broad-run farms will be impacted positively by this. Item 10, Riptide Square, this is kicking off a process through which the county will remove the remnants of a burned townhouse that has not been cleaned up by the owner or by the insurance company.

This was an arson case, which kind of tied things up, and then also dealing with the insurance company has tied things up, and this neighborhood has been dealing with a carcass of a townhouse pretty close to Lowe's Island Elementary School. And so this starts the process by which the county can go in and clean up that mess, for lack of a better word, and make the place look a little better for the community, a little safer for the community.

And then the county will be asking for reimbursement through a lien on the property once we have paid for the cleanup. Item 11, Resolution of Intent to Amend—oh, I'm sorry, never mind, I don't want to talk about that.

It has been just such an honor and a pleasure to be in this group of 15 people who are, you know, very, very impressive human beings, to talk about how to get trust back into public health.

Unfortunately, after COVID, a lot of trust was lost in public health. But we did talk about the fact that public health hasn't just done vaccinations. They've done the whole campaign for seatbelts was a public health campaign. The campaign against smoking was a public health campaign.

I think Amy Anderson, actually, her grandson still lives in Loudoun County.

She was an educator in our county. Yeah, yeah. Absolutely. What does the Burke Family Reunion Club have planned for Juneteenth this year? We have a great day planned. Okay. We have a lot of great live entertainment. We have food vendors, merchant vendors.

We'll have activities for young children. And it's considered a family-friendly event. And we encourage any and everyone to come out and partake in what we call the greatest day of the year, Juneteenth. I love that you say it's a family-friendly event and that Juneteenth belongs to everybody.

It is an opportunity to preserve history, celebrate culture, strengthen community, and inspire future generations.

It reminds us that freedom should never be taken for granted and that every generation has a responsibility to learn from the past while working toward a brighter future. Could not agree more. And then finally, what is the best way for people to contact you all to learn more about the Burke Family Reunion Club?

How can they get involved with your contact information in general? Yes, we do have a website, and our website is www.thebfrc.com. You can reach me through the website. There's a way that you can send messages through the website so they come to me.

We're always looking for folks to join us and help us in any event that we put on, because we do a lot in the community, not just in Leesburg, throughout the entire county. This class is a special needs teacher as well. It is a special person who can do that job, so thank you for doing that. Absolutely. Well, one more time, give the website. www.thebfrc.com.

I think you're doing a great job, and I do think that Juneteenth is a holiday that belongs to everyone, if they really understand it. They are explosive devices that can cause serious injury and property damage if not handled correctly. The safest way to enjoy fireworks is to attend a public display conducted by trained professionals. The Fire Marshal's Office provides a comprehensive list of public fireworks displays in our area along with safety information at loudon.gov slash fireworks.

Limited walk-ins will be available at the health clinic at the Shenandoah Building here in Leesburg. Appointments are strongly recommended. This report is provided pursuing the board's 2023 equity resolution and summarizes the county's progress during FY26, including the implementation of the Loudon Equity Action Plan and advancement of board-directed initiatives and priorities for FY27.

FY26 represented an important transition for the county. Following the establishment of foundational frameworks, assessments, and planning efforts in prior years, the county shifted its focus from framework development to implementation. During the fiscal year, efforts centered on integrating the board's priorities into governance structures, departmental planning, performance management, and service delivery, while establishing systems to support accountability and measurable outcomes.

Together, these focus areas reflect a coordinated countywide approach to strengthening organizational effectiveness, improving accountability, and supporting responsive service delivery. Tonight we have six slides covering items number seven on the agenda, titled the County's Residential Traffic Management Guide Update. For some background, in September 2019, the board endorsed the county's Residential Traffic Management Guide, also commonly known as the RTM Guide.

This guide was developed through a board member initiative in 2017 to create a more organized and consistent approach for evaluating and addressing traffic safety concerns in residential neighborhoods. It established a uniform set of criteria for roads that are VDOT maintained with posted speed limits of 25 miles per hour or less.

At a high level, the process relies on input from residents, county staff, VDOT, Loudoun County Sheriff's Office, Loudoun County Public Schools, the Fire and Rescue Department, and other stakeholders to help identify traffic concerns and develop appropriate solutions. The RTM guide consists of two programs, the traffic calming and the cut-through traffic.

The traffic calming focuses on addressing speeding concerns by evaluating existing traffic conditions and identifying the appropriate mitigation measures. And the cut-through traffic looks at drivers who use a neighborhood as a shortcut, meaning that they enter and exit the community without having a destination or origin within it.

This particular graphic on the right illustrates that the types of traffic safety concerns that DTSI regularly receives, as well as the various sources of those concerns. And typically, these concerns are addressed through a three-pronged approach, education, enforcement, and engineering.
